outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the general conjecture has been claimed proved twice, both in 2026 and both restricted to second-countable groups and manifolds: in an OpenAI preprint (dated 23 September 2026, released 6 October 2026) and in a preprint by 'A. Dabrowski's AI agents' (dated 8 October 2026, with a Lean formalisation of a second-countable C∞ variant). Neither claim has a human mathematical reading in the record, an automated audit reports a breaking step in both, and the DeepMind formal-conjectures entry for the problem remained open on the record date. The only earlier in-window result is Shelukhin's symplectic-category preprint (March 2024), which settles a restricted case.
problem_asks: (1) The groups: every locally compact topological group G. The statement adds no Hausdorff, second-countability or connectedness assumption on G. (2) The spaces: every topological manifold M. The statement names no dimension, connectedness, second-countability or boundary condition; by standard convention M is finite-dimensional. (3) The hypothesis: a continuous action of G on M that is faithful. (4) The conclusion, for every such triple: G is a Lie group. This is one universal claim over all (G, M, action); no part is a special case. The Wikipedia article (fetched 2026) gives a reduction that is not part of the statement: by the Gleason–Yamabe and Newman theorems it suffices that, for each prime p, the p-adic integers ℤₚ admit no faithful continuous action on a connected finite-dimensional manifold. A result that proves only a restriction of (1) to (4), such as second-countable groups, a C∞ rather than analytic conclusion, or a symplectic setting, leaves the rest open.

events.what_happened: Bochner and Montgomery proved the Lie conclusion for effective actions by differentiable transformations: 'Locally compact groups of differentiable transformations', Annals of Mathematics 47 (1946), 639–653 (per a search result). The same authors' 1945 Annals paper, 'Groups of differentiable and real or complex analytic transformations' (vol. 46, 685–694), is also cited. Neither Annals paper was opened. One search summary gives 1943 for the same result and calls it an error. Recorded as a pre-window solution of a restricted (smooth-action) case.
events.delivers: The full conclusion (G is a Lie group) for groups acting effectively by differentiable transformations on a manifold, per search-summary description; the exact regularity class was not checked against the paper.
events.remains: Actions that are only continuous, Lipschitz, Hölder, quasiconformal, or otherwise non-differentiable; the general statement.
events.time_since_posted: about 80 years; classical and cited as settled; the 1946 paper itself was not checked
events.direction: Proves the conjecture for the smooth-action case (in the direction the conjecture asserts).

events.what_happened: Montgomery and Zippin settled the case of two-dimensional manifolds. Per a search result the material is collected in their monograph 'Topological Transformation Groups' (1955); the original two-dimensional argument was not located, so the true date may be earlier than 1955. Pardon's 2018 survey (arXiv 1811.08748; abstract opened) says it 'include[s] a proof of it in dimension two' and attributes the dimension-two case to Montgomery and Zippin; a search summary of Pardon's text cites Montgomery–Zippin at [17, p. 249].
events.delivers: The full statement, for manifolds of dimension two only (Pardon's survey abstract confirms the dimension-two case).
events.remains: Dimension three (settled by Pardon in 2013 for three-manifolds) and dimension four and above (open).

checked_by.qualification: Topologist; author of the 2013 JAMS paper on the three-dimensional case
checked_by.what_they_did: Gave a self-contained proof of the dimension-two case in a 2018 survey, crediting Montgomery–Zippin

events.direction: Proves the conjecture in dimension two (in the direction the conjecture asserts).

events.what_happened: S. M. Ageev, 'Classifying spaces for free actions, and the Hilbert–Smith conjecture', Matematicheskii Sbornik 183(1) (1992), 143–151 (per a mathnet search result; full text not opened). Per the abstract summary, free actions of a zero-dimensional compact group on the n-dimensional Menger compactum are universal for free actions, and a non-existence result for equivariant maps between Menger compacta of different dimensions would imply the Hilbert–Smith conjecture when the orbit space is finite-dimensional. This is a neighbouring question (free actions on compacta with a dimension assumption), not the conjecture as stated.
events.delivers: No resolution of the conjecture. A reduction of a weak version (finite-dimensional orbit space) to a non-existence statement about equivariant maps, which Ageev conjectured and which Chirvasitu–Dąbrowski–Tobolski treat (see their event).
events.remains: The conjecture in full, and the weak version's equivariant non-existence statement.
events.time_since_posted: about 34 years; its conjecture is used by later work but the 1992 paper itself was not checked
events.direction: Neutral; sets up a route to a weak version, not a result on the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Dušan Repovš and Evgenij Ščepin, 'A proof of the Hilbert–Smith conjecture for actions by Lipschitz maps', Mathematische Annalen 308 (1997), 361–364 (per a search result). The authors' PDF copy was fetched but its binary text could not be extracted, so the paper's wording was not verified. The Wikipedia article (fetched 2026) states the result: the conjecture holds for groups acting by Lipschitz maps on a Riemannian manifold, using covering, fractal and cohomological dimension theory.
events.delivers: The full conclusion for effective actions by Lipschitz maps on a Riemannian manifold (per Wikipedia).
events.remains: Actions that are not Lipschitz, which is the general case.
events.direction: Proves the conjecture for Lipschitz actions (in the direction the conjecture asserts).

events.what_happened: Jože Malešič (spelled Maleshich, Maleshick and Iozke in arXiv citations; the COBISS record gives Malešič, Jože), 'The Hilbert–Smith conjecture for Hölder actions', Russian Mathematical Surveys 52(2) (1997), 407–408 (per search results; not opened). A search summary of the Slovenian abstract says the conjecture is proved when the homeomorphisms are Hölder with exponent at least m/(m+2), m the manifold dimension; a search summary of Pardon's survey states the threshold as C^{0, n/(n+2)+ε}, a slightly different formulation.
events.delivers: The full conclusion for effective Hölder actions above the stated exponent threshold (per search-summary description).
events.remains: Hölder actions with lower regularity and the general case.
events.doubts: The exponent threshold is stated differently in the two sources the search summaries cite (m/(m+2) in the Slovenian abstract; n/(n+2)+ε in Pardon's survey); not resolved.
events.direction: Proves the conjecture for a regularity class (in the direction the conjecture asserts).

events.what_happened: Gaven Martin, 'The Hilbert–Smith conjecture for quasiconformal actions', Electronic Research Announcements of the AMS 5 (1999), 66–70 (per search results). It is an announcement. The announced claim: a locally compact group of quasiconformal homeomorphisms acting effectively on a Riemannian manifold is a Lie group. The EMIS copy returned HTTP 503 and the AMS page was not opened. Search summaries say the manuscript is dated 9 November 1998, that the note refers to a companion paper in preparation, and that it was posted 28 May 1999; the AMS URL carries the date 1999-05-09. Recorded as an announcement with the month the sources agree on.
events.revisions: Manuscript dated 9 Nov 1998 (per search summary); ERA-AMS path date 9 May 1999; posting date 28 May 1999 (per search summary). Day not settled.
events.delivers: Announced: the full conclusion for effective actions by quasiconformal homeomorphisms on a Riemannian manifold. Per a search summary the note says the result holds 'in somewhat more generality' than stated; that generality was not checked.
events.remains: Actions that are not quasiconformal; the general statement. The announced result is not established by the record because the companion full paper was not located.
events.time_since_posted: about 27 years; no full paper located
events.doubts: Announcement only. The companion paper that the note refers to was not located in any search. Wikipedia (fetched 2026) lists it as a known result and says it was used for unique analytic continuation of Beltrami systems, but that is a citation, not a check of the argument.
events.direction: Announces the conjecture for quasiconformal actions (in the direction the conjecture asserts).

events.what_happened: Louis F. McAuley (Binghamton University), companion arXiv preprint 'The Hilbert-Smith Conjecture' (math/0103145, math.GT). Per the fetched abstract summary, it reduces the conjecture to showing that a p-adic group cannot act effectively on a compact connected n-manifold, shows this for free actions, notes that fixed points add complexity, and defers the general case to a later paper. Eight versions, 23 March to 7 December 2001. The comments list edits on pages 6–8, 16–17, 22, 24 and 28. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: The free-action case only: per the summary, no p-adic group acts freely on a compact connected n-manifold. The fixed-point case is not claimed.
events.remains: The fixed-point (non-free) case and therefore the conjecture as stated.
events.time_since_posted: about 25 years; no journal record and no published engagement found
events.doubts: The author's own abstract (per the summary) defers the general case, so this companion does not claim the full result. Its relation to math/0103215 by the same author, which claims the full result, is not explained in the record.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in the free-action special case, if the argument is sound; not checked.

events.what_happened: Louis F. McAuley, 'A Proof of the Hilbert-Smith Conjecture' (arXiv math/0103215, math.GT). The abstract restates the conjecture and says the author gives a 'rather straightforward proof' (wording from a search-result copy of the abstract; the fetch summary says 'fairly direct'). It builds on Cernavskii's results on finite-to-one maps, extending them to orbit maps of effective p-adic group actions on compact connected n-manifolds, and says Smith theory is not used. Eight versions from 29 March to 7 December 2001. The arXiv comments list only minor edits. No journal reference on the arXiv page. The paper body was not read.
events.revisions: v1 29 Mar 2001; v2 23 Apr 2001; v3 15 May 2001; v4 2 Jul 2001; v5 9 Jul 2001; v6 1 Aug 2001; v7 8 Aug 2001; v8 7 Dec 2001 (current). Comments: minor readability edits only.
events.delivers: Claims the full conjecture: every locally compact group acting effectively on a connected manifold is a Lie group. The abstract places the argument in the orbit-map route described above. Whether the body covers fixed points was not checked.
events.remains: Nothing if the claim holds. The companion preprint (math/0103145) says fixed points add complexity, so the coverage of the full claim is unverified.
events.time_since_posted: about 25 years; no journal record and no published engagement found
events.doubts: (1) No journal publication, referee report or published commentary on the arXiv page or in any search. (2) The companion preprint by the same author says it proves only the free-action case and defers the general case, so the full claim here has no support in the companion. (3) The Wikipedia article (fetched 2026) lists the conjecture among open problems and does not mention McAuley. (4) ProofAtlas (dated 7 Aug 2026) lists the conjecture as open and names no claimed proof; a search summary of Pardon's 2018 survey calls the conjecture the main open problem.
events.direction: Claims the conjecture is true (every such group is a Lie group).

events.what_happened: John Pardon, 'The Hilbert–Smith conjecture for three-manifolds' (arXiv 1112.2324). The v1 abstract, posted 11 December 2011, reads: 'We show that there is no faithful action of ℤₚ (the p-adic integers) on a connected three-manifold.' Method per the fetched abstract summary: assume such an action; find a ℤₚ-invariant open set U with H₂(U) = ℤ; find an incompressible surface in U whose isotopy class is fixed by ℤₚ; derive a contradiction from the induced homomorphism ℤₚ → MCG(F). Version 2 is dated 10 April 2012 and version 3 (current) 22 January 2013, whose abstract states the full result: every locally compact group acting faithfully on a connected three-manifold is a Lie group. Published as J. Amer. Math. Soc. 26 (2013), no. 3, 879–899 (DOI 10.1090/S0894-0347-2013-00766-3). The v1 and v2 abstracts were not separately read; the v1 wording quoted above is from the v1 abstract page.
events.revisions: v1 11 Dec 2011 (abstract: Z_p exclusion only); v2 10 Apr 2012; v3 22 Jan 2013 (abstract: full Lie statement for three-manifolds; comment 'to appear in Journal of the AMS'); JAMS 26(3) 2013.
events.delivers: Full conclusion for three-manifolds: every locally compact group acting faithfully on a connected three-manifold is a Lie group (v3 abstract). The reduction from the full conjecture to ℤₚ (Wikipedia; Pardon) makes the v1 Z_p exclusion equivalent to this, but the v1 abstract itself states only the Z_p exclusion.
events.remains: Manifolds of dimension four and above; the general conjecture.

checked_by.qualification: Topologist; author of a Bourbaki seminar exposé
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a Bourbaki seminar exposé (Astérisque 390, 2017) covering the three-dimensional case, in French (per a search result; not opened)

events.doubts: Scope grew between versions: the v1 abstract claims only the ℤₚ exclusion on a connected three-manifold and the v3 abstract claims the full Lie statement. The record does not show a dispute about the step; the reduction is standard and Pardon states it in v3.
events.direction: Proves the conjecture in dimension three (in the direction the conjecture asserts).

events.what_happened: Alexander Dranishnikov, 'On some problems related to the Hilbert-Smith conjecture' (arXiv 1504.07277). Abstract: 'We present a reduction of the Hilbert-Smith conjecture in the case of the finite dimensional orbit space to some algebraic topology problems.' Versions: 27 April 2015 (v1), 1 March 2016 (v2), 1 July 2016 (v3, current). No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: A reduction only, of the case where the orbit space is finite-dimensional, to unnamed algebraic topology problems. No conclusion for the conjecture as stated.
events.remains: The whole conjecture; the reduced algebraic-topology problems.
events.time_since_posted: about 11 years; no journal record or published engagement found in the record
events.direction: Neutral; a reduction of a restricted (finite-dimensional orbit space) version.

events.what_happened: Alexandru Chirvasitu and Benjamin Passer, 'Compact Group Actions on Topological and Noncommutative Joins' (arXiv 1604.02173). It studies the Type 1 and Type 2 noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam conjectures of Baum, Dąbrowski and Hajac, giving a reduction of Type 1 and counterexamples to Type 2 for classical groups. Versions: 7 April 2016 (v1), 27 April 2016, 2 February 2017, 2 September 2017 (v4). Journal reference Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 146 (2018), 3217–3232 (per the arXiv page). This is a neighbouring problem, recorded to show the chain of weak-version results; it is not about the Hilbert–Smith conjecture directly.
events.delivers: Noncommutative Borsuk–Ulam results (Type 1 reduction; Type 2 counterexamples for classical groups). The arXiv abstract does not state a topological Baum–Dąbrowski–Hajac result proved by these authors, which a search summary had attributed to them.
events.remains: Not applicable to the Hilbert–Smith conjecture as stated.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (referee process)

events.doubts: A search summary of Chirvasitu–Dąbrowski–Tobolski says a later revision of their paper traces an error to this paper's topological result. The arXiv page for this paper (read as fetched) states no error or correction, so the two sources conflict and the claim was not confirmed.
events.direction: Neighbouring result; not on the Hilbert–Smith conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Alexandru Chirvasitu, Ludwik Dąbrowski and Mariusz Tobolski, arXiv 1612.09567. First version 30 December 2016 (a search summary gives the first title as 'Equivariant rigidity of Menger compacta and the Hilbert–Smith conjecture'); version 2 5 March 2017; version 3 14 September 2018 under the title 'The weak Hilbert-Smith conjecture from a Borsuk-Ulam-type conjecture'. The v3 abstract (fetched) states that they prove the Baum–Dąbrowski–Hajac conjecture for locally trivial principal G-bundles, that this partially settles a conjecture of Ageev, and that Ageev's conjecture implies a weak form of the Hilbert–Smith conjecture: no infinite compact zero-dimensional group acts freely on a manifold with finite-dimensional orbit space. Comments: 'significant new result added'. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.revisions: v1 30 Dec 2016 (per search summary, first title 'Equivariant rigidity of Menger compacta and the Hilbert-Smith conjecture'); v2 5 Mar 2017; v3 14 Sep 2018 (current).
events.delivers: The weak form only (free actions of an infinite compact zero-dimensional group on a manifold with finite-dimensional orbit space). Per the v3 abstract this rests on the BDH result for locally trivial bundles and on Ageev's conjecture, which is partial.
events.remains: The full conjecture; the weak form's chain (BDH → Ageev → weak form) is not established as complete by the record.
events.time_since_posted: about 10 years; no journal record found
events.doubts: Sources conflict on the history of the claim. A search summary says v1 presented the weak result as proved outright, using a Borsuk–Ulam theorem, and that a later revision makes the main result conditional on the BDH conjecture after an error in arXiv 1604.02173. The v3 abstract fetched here says the BDH conjecture is proved for locally trivial bundles and says nothing about an error or a condition. Not resolved.
events.direction: Partial result toward a weak version; neutral on the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: John Pardon, 'Totally disconnected groups (not) acting on two-manifolds' (arXiv 1811.08748). Abstract: 'We briefly survey the Hilbert--Smith Conjecture, and we include a proof of it in dimension two.' Posted 21 November 2018. A search summary gives its venue as Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 102 (Georgia International Topology Conference 2017), 187–193; not opened.
events.delivers: A survey, and a self-contained proof of the dimension-two case, already attributed to Montgomery–Zippin. Not a new result.
events.remains: Dimension three and above (as the conjecture stands in the survey).
events.direction: Proves the dimension-two case (in the direction the conjecture asserts); survey of the conjecture as open.

events.what_happened: Michael Levin, 'Resolving compacta by free p-adic actions' (arXiv 1909.12648), posted 27 September 2019. It studies compacta that can be resolved by a free p-adic action on a lower-dimensional compactum, with cohomological dimension over ℤ[1/p] equal to 1. A search summary gives a Fundamenta Mathematicae 255 (2021) publication, not opened. It concerns compacta, not manifolds, and does not mention the Hilbert–Smith conjecture on the abstract page.
events.delivers: Results on free p-adic actions on compacta. Not about manifolds and not about the Hilbert–Smith conjecture as stated.
events.remains: Not applicable to the conjecture as stated.
events.direction: Neighbouring result; neutral on the conjecture as stated.

events.what_happened: Egor Shelukhin, 'A symplectic Hilbert-Smith conjecture' (arXiv 2403.07195), with an appendix by Leonid Polterovich. Version 1 was posted 11 March 2024 and version 2 on 26 June 2024 (comments: 18 pages; modifications of Remarks 9, 19 and Example 20). The fetched summary of the abstract says it proves new cases for actions by natural homeomorphisms in symplectic topology: the p-adic integers admit no nontrivial continuous action by Hamiltonian homeomorphisms on symplectically aspherical manifolds; and, for a class including standard symplectic tori, a locally compact group acting faithfully by homeomorphisms in the C⁰ closure of time-one maps of symplectic isotopies must be a Lie group. Methods: barcodes and power operations in Floer cohomology; they also apply to Hofer's metric. Polterovich's appendix derives obstructions for Hamiltonian actions by semisimple p-adic analytic groups. No journal reference on the arXiv page. An IAS Symplectic Geometry Seminar talk on 6 May 2024 covered the same material (a talk, not an assessment).
events.delivers: Restricted cases in the symplectic category: no nontrivial continuous Hamiltonian action of ℤₚ on symplectically aspherical manifolds; and, for a class including standard tori, the Lie conclusion for groups acting in the C⁰ closure of symplectic isotopies. Scope is the symplectic/Hamiltonian setting, not arbitrary topological actions.
events.remains: The general conjecture for arbitrary continuous faithful actions on topological manifolds; actions outside the Hamiltonian or C⁰-symplectic setting; manifolds outside the symplectically aspherical class.
events.time_since_posted: about 2.6 years since v1; no journal reference and no citing paper found in the record
events.direction: Proves restricted (symplectic-category) cases in the direction the conjecture asserts; does not decide the general case.

events.what_happened: An undated-in-text blog post on ppalme.wordpress.com, dated by its URL to 9 September 2026 (titled 'Beyond Pardon's 3-Manifold Theorem: Reframing Hilbert–Smith via ℤₚ Small-Subgroup Towers, Yang Dimension Jumps, and Codimension-One Carriers'). The author gives no name in the visible text. It proposes a 'topological gap principle' framing and a 'Machine-Assisted Lemma Discovery Program' as future work, and states that 'As of 2026, the general conjecture remains open.' It claims no proof. The page is a 204,558-character text of which the first 100,000 characters were read.
events.delivers: Nothing established; frameworks and candidate lemmas, no theorem.
events.remains: The whole conjecture.
events.direction: No claim of a result; proposes research directions.

events.what_happened: OpenAI released a 46-page preprint, 'The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension' (file preprints/The-Hilbert-Smith-conjecture-in-every-finite-dimension-September-23-2026/paper.pdf in the public repository github.com/openai/math, commit adc7f12). The README of that preprint gives the author as 'OpenAI', the date as 'September 23, 2026', and the citation as an 'OpenAI Math Release preprint'. The repository was made public with 722 manuscripts (719 after three withdrawals) on 6 October 2026, per press and the repository README; the paper's own date is 23 September 2026, and several other manuscripts in the release also carry September dates (kingy.ai). The paper claims: every locally compact, second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected, Hausdorff, second-countable, finite-dimensional topological manifold without boundary is a Lie group. The paper's PDF text was not extracted (the binary fetch failed), so its argument, contribution statement and acknowledgements were not read. The openai/math repository's own README (fetched, summarised by the fetch tool) says the manuscripts are 'produced by an internal OpenAI model' and that 'the vast majority of results were obtained with the same procedure using an unreleased internal OpenAI model'; it says 'some of the unformalized results could have issues'. The DeepMind issue (#6914) and the Vibemathed tracker both report that no Lean proof is included for this paper. A third-party index (kisonecat) lists it as family 304, 'The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension'.
events.revisions: Paper's self-date 23 Sep 2026; public repository release 6 Oct 2026 (Retraction Watch, kingy.ai, Nature via search summary). Three other manuscripts were withdrawn on 7 Oct 2026 for a sign error (not this one, per Retraction Watch); fourteen others were revised (whether this paper is among them was not checked). No version history for this paper is visible on the repository page.
events.delivers: Claims the conjecture in the second-countable setting: for every locally compact, second-countable Hausdorff G acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected, Hausdorff, second-countable, finite-dimensional manifold without boundary, G is a Lie group. This is the full Lie conclusion for all finite dimensions, under those hypotheses.
events.remains: Groups that are locally compact but not second-countable (the DeepMind issue says the reduction 'needs an argument'); the bullet's bare 'topological manifold' wording against the paper's connected, second-countable, boundaryless hypotheses (not assessed here); and any gap in the paper's argument, which the record does not settle.

events.doubts: (1) No public verification by a mathematician who works on transformation groups or Smith theory was found; the Pardon search returned no comment from Pardon on this paper. (2) No Lean proof is included for this paper (DeepMind issue #6914; Vibemathed). (3) Scope: the proof concerns second-countable groups and manifolds and connected, boundaryless manifolds; the DeepMind issue says the group reduction needs an argument; the Lean variant (PR #7043) also concludes a C∞ rather than analytic Lie structure. (4) The Cursor-based audit reports that the chart/Newman step is where its sponge case breaks and calls the scoping correct; it lists no FAIL in the OpenAI targeted audit and does not list chart/Newman among the WEAK items. Its visible text does not explain the step, and the PDFs behind it were not visible, so the disagreement is not resolved. (5) The release's README says some unformalized results 'could have issues'. (6) Retraction Watch reports three other manuscripts withdrawn for a sign error on 7 Oct 2026; this paper is not among them, per that article. (7) A Scientific American quote says OpenAI 'did not include full prompts or run-time details for how their agents uncovered the proofs'. (8) The paper's own date (23 Sep) and public release (6 Oct) differ; this record uses the release date as the first public appearance.
events.direction: Claims to prove the conjecture in the second-countable setting, i.e., in the direction the conjecture asserts (every such group is Lie). No counterexample is claimed.

events.what_happened: GitHub issue #6914 in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, 'HilbertProblems/5: the Hilbert–Smith conjecture is true', opened 7 October 2026 by mo271, labelled 'hilbert-problems' and 'solution found'. It flags the declarations hilbert_smith_conjecture and hilbert_smith_padic_formulation in FormalConjectures/HilbertProblems/5.lean, tagged 'research open', as apparently settled by the OpenAI preprint. It notes that no Lean proof is included in the release, that the formal statements do not assume second countability of G or X, and that for the p-adic formulation this is 'routine' while for the group statement 'the reduction needs an argument'. It suggests marking both 'research solved' and citing the paper after settling the second-countability question. It carries the disclaimer 'prepared with AI assistance and may contain mistakes'. No comments on the fetch date beyond the labels. Status on the record date: Open. The file on main still tags both declarations 'research open' with proof 'sorry' (fetched).

events.remains: Everything: the issue is not a proof and the formal declarations remain 'research open' on main.
events.doubts: Not a verification: it flags a scope gap and does not check the paper's argument. Its own disclaimer says it was prepared with AI assistance.

events.what_happened: GitHub account adbrw published the repository adbrw/HS_proof (About: 'Hilbert-Smith proof'), containing a 17-page PDF, 'Integral tail signatures and the Hilbert–Smith conjecture', whose author line reads 'A. Dabrowski's AI agents' and whose date is 'October 8, 2026'. Theorem 1.1 (as the README states it): for every prime p, a continuous action of ℤₚ on a connected finite-dimensional manifold has nontrivial kernel. Corollary 1.2: a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group acting continuously and effectively on such a manifold 'is a Lie group with its given topology'. The Corollary is said to follow from Theorem 1.1 by 'the standard reduction to p-adic exclusion' using locally compact group structure and Newman's theorem. The Lean part: Challenge.lean states hilbert_smith with a sorry proof; Solution.lean claims to prove the same statement as HSFormal.hilbertSmith n M G (a library of 239 modules). The README gives expected verifier outputs ('Your solution is okay!' for Comparator; 'SafeVerify check passed.' for SafeVerify) and claimed axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; the fetch shows expected outputs, not run results. The PDF itself was not read. The identity of 'A. Dabrowski' is not established in the record; the GitHub handle does not name the author.
events.revisions: PDF dated 8 Oct 2026 (17 pp.); the repository has 12 commits, undated on the page. The PR that formalises a variant (#7043, 9 Oct 2026) cites the paper as dated 8 Oct 2026.

disputes.summary: Two 2026 claims of the general conjecture exist: the OpenAI preprint (dated 23 Sep 2026, public 6 Oct 2026) and the Dabrowski preprint (dated 8 Oct 2026). The audit says they share an approach and that neither is Pardon's or Yang's argument. No public priority dispute between them was found.

Chirvasitu–Dąbrowski–Tobolski (arXiv 1612.09567): a search summary says v1 presented the weak Hilbert–Smith result as proved and a later revision makes it conditional on the BDH conjecture after an error in arXiv 1604.02173. The v3 abstract read here states the BDH result for locally trivial bundles and mentions no error. Chirvasitu–Passer's arXiv page (1604.02173) also states no error. Unresolved.

Pardon (arXiv 1112.2324): the v1 abstract states only the ℤₚ exclusion on a connected three-manifold; the v3 abstract states the full Lie statement for three-manifolds. Both appear in the same arXiv record; the reduction is standard.

Status disagreement: the Wikipedia article (fetched 2026) and ProofAtlas (dated 7 Aug 2026) list the conjecture as open; the OpenAI preprint and the Dabrowski repository claim it settled in the second-countable setting; the DeepMind formal-conjectures file on main still tags both declarations 'research open' at the record date, and PR #7043 proposing 'research solved' remains open.

Identity of 'A. Dabrowski' (credited with 'AI agents' on the adbrw repository) is not established. Ludwik Dąbrowski co-authored arXiv 1612.09567 (weak version) but the record does not show that the two are the same person.

The OpenAI preprint's own date (23 Sep 2026) and its first public appearance (6 Oct 2026, repository release) differ. The Vibemathed tracker uses 23 Sep 2026 as its 'solved' date. This record uses 6 Oct 2026 as the first public appearance and gives the paper date in the revisions field.

summary: The record has three sources of post-2024 activity and a long pre-window literature. The only in-window partial result is Shelukhin's symplectic-category preprint (arXiv 2403.07195, posted 11 March 2024; v2 26 June 2024), which proves that ℤₚ has no nontrivial continuous Hamiltonian action on symplectically aspherical manifolds and derives the Lie conclusion for a class including standard tori; the arXiv page lists no journal reference and I found no citing paper. The 2026 activity consists of two AI-attributed claims of the general conjecture restricted to second-countable groups and manifolds. (a) OpenAI's preprint 'The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension' (46 pages; author line 'OpenAI'; paper date 23 September 2026; first public appearance 6 October 2026 in the openai/math repository). The repository's README says its manuscripts were produced by an unreleased internal OpenAI model and that 'some of the unformalized results could have issues'; the README names no paper, but the exceptions it lists do not include this one. I could not extract the PDF text, so the paper's own argument, contribution statement and acknowledgements were not read; the attribution to this paper therefore rests on the repository-wide statement and on the paper's silence about its process. (b) 'Integral tail signatures and the Hilbert–Smith conjecture' by the GitHub account adbrw, credited to 'A. Dabrowski's AI agents', dated 8 October 2026, with a Lean 4 artefact that proves a second-countable C∞ variant; the PR carrying that variant (#7043, open) was approved by one reviewer who reproduced the Comparator run, but that check covers the Lean statements, not the PDF's mathematics. Neither claim has a public reading by a mathematician who works on transformation groups in the record. The DeepMind issue #6914 (7 October) flagged the OpenAI paper and its second-countability gap; the issue, like the audit, carries an AI-assistance note. The Cursor-based audit (ajjcoppola) reports that the chart/Newman step breaks in the sponge case of the OpenAI preprint and in the Dabrowski preprint; it is a single undefined-grade AI critique with its PDFs not visible, so it is recorded as a lead, not a verdict. Close calls: whether the second-countability and connectedness restrictions (and the C∞ conclusion in Lean) are harmless or are gaps the bullet's wording does not allow; whether the OpenAI paper's AI attribution applies to it specifically (it does on the repository's own statement, not on its own text); and whether the audit's chart/Newman objection is correct, which the record cannot settle. Pre-window history: Bochner–Montgomery (smooth actions, 1946), Montgomery–Zippin (dimension two, monograph 1955, date of original argument not pinned), Ageev (1992; neighbouring), Repovš–Ščepin (Lipschitz, 1997), Malešič (Hölder, 1997), Martin (quasiconformal announcement, 1999; companion not located), McAuley (two 2001 preprints; the full-claim one has no journal or uptake record in 25 years, and its companion says only free actions are handled), Pardon (three-manifolds, arXiv 11 Dec 2011, JAMS 2013; the v1 abstract states only the ℤₚ exclusion, v3 the full statement), and Pardon's 2018 survey re-proving dimension two. Weak-version and neighbouring work (Dranishnikov 2015; Chirvasitu–Passer 2016; Chirvasitu–Dąbrowski–Tobolski 2016; Levin 2019; ppalme 2026 blog) is recorded and discounted. No Quanta or Tao article on this problem was found; Tao reposted the AHM statement on 7 October 2026, which names no result. Retraction Watch reports three OpenAI manuscripts withdrawn on 7 October for a sign error, none of them on this topic. Status trackers list the OpenAI result as 'Candidate (review pending)' and 'Unreviewed' (VibeMathed) and the problem as open as of 7 August (ProofAtlas). The current Wikipedia article's most recent progress is Pardon's 2013 dimension-three result and it gives no current status.
competing_reading: The strongest case that the 2026 claims should count as settling the conjecture: connectedness and second countability are standard hypotheses in topological manifold theory and the Wikipedia reduction to ℤₚ goes through them; the DeepMind thread itself calls the p-adic version 'routine'; the Lean variant has been checked by Comparator and reproduced by a reviewer; the only technical critique is a single AI-driven audit with undefined grades and no visible argument, and for the OpenAI paper it lists no FAIL and no chart/Newman WEAK item, reading the sponge failure as a correctly scoped boundary. The strongest case against: no mathematician who works in this area has publicly read either argument; the OpenAI paper has no Lean proof; the Dabrowski Lean artefact proves a C∞ variant, the author concedes a missing C∞→Cω step of over 10,000 lines, and the same release has already withdrawn three manuscripts for a sign error; the repository says some unformalised results 'could have issues'; the closest analogue in this record, McAuley's 2001 claim, was never accepted in 25 years; and the 2011 Pardon case shows the restrictions can change between versions. On the restricted symplectic result (Shelukhin 2024) the strongest reading is that it is a real but partial advance that does not touch the general conjecture.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A readable copy of the OpenAI paper's text, checked by topologists who work on transformation groups or Smith theory, with a statement of whether the chart/Newman step holds. (2) A public response from the authors to the audit's chart/Newman objection, or a published correction. (3) An independent Lean build of the OpenAI main theorem; the release says none is included for this paper. (4) For the Dabrowski claim, a human reading of the PDF's signature/integrality argument and the chart step, plus the Comparator run retained and reproduced by someone other than the reviewer. (5) The outcome of PR #7043 and issue #6914 (merge, or a stated reason to keep 'research open'), and an argument for the non-second-countable case. (6) For McAuley, any published acceptance or refutation, or a citation by Pardon's 2013 paper or 2018 survey with a verdict. (7) Post-2024 citations of Shelukhin's paper in a journal or arXiv listing, and a check of whether its symplectic cases extend to other manifold classes.
